decision: In-game prop: a large blue sci-fi containment tube for Snow Fortress, generated by TRELLIS.2 (same generator and treatment as the walls, container and box). Closed object with depth (relief 0.93), a tall cylinder seen from any angle, so a mesh prop. The raw mesh was 25,000 disconnected shards and carried clutter the design does not want: a floor cable tangle, a flat plate, a bottle, a second canister and loose wires, plus an opaque pale slab where the glass should be. tools/blender/prepare_bluetube.py removes those by position (measured from orthographic renders of THIS file, not general rules) and puts a cylinder of blue smoke where the glass was. The smoke is part of the one mesh and takes its colour from a patch of the base-colour atlas painted bright cyan in texture space the deleted glass freed up; it is not transparent and does not animate. scene_kit then builds it 12.1 studs tall (8.9 x 9.1), bottom pivot, decimated to 9,000 triangles in one mesh; the tile advice is overridden as for the other props. Textures converted from 2048 WebP to 1024 PNG; verified in a textured render that the smoke still reads cyan after decimation and downscale. If a glowing or animated look is wanted in game, add a Neon part or ParticleEmitter in Studio, since a single imported mesh cannot be partly Neon. Scenery by default; if made cover it is a collidable prop the layout gates cannot audit.
